expected_return.window: scorebord: BUY 13:30 ET on the entry day; SELL amc at the next open, bmo at 13:00 ET on the report day; gross

note: Each member is reported as a percentile of its own live range, 0-100 (pct), with its direction in side; panel_pct (0-100) is the size of the mean of the signed percentiles and side its direction; panel_pct_sd their spread. The selection is panel_pct in the top 20%. panel_score is the signed median of the members' sizes, each read against its own recent history. consensus_k counts members that put the name in their own top 20% on the panel's side; that, not sign agreement, is what selected well on the development names. Certainty (p_up) is recorded and decides nothing. expected_edge_pct is a shrunk in-sample prior, not a forecast. Research only.

opus5.note: Item 0 is the strongest thing in the three packs on paper - the FY guide's own 18.25-18.50 MXN assumption, sourced from Cemex's 6-K, against a 17.1-17.8 actual while 14 analysts updated on 2026-10-12 still sit at the guide floor - but it is cut roughly in half because analysts updating on 10-12 could see spot FX for the whole quarter (so the floor consensus plausibly prices underlying slippage, not an overlooked tailwind), the peso had weakened back to 17.78 by 09-28 (the searcher wrongly binned that as a duplicate rather than letting it shrink the finding), and this name sold a Q2 beat-and-raise -3.6%; items 2 and 1 (no Q3 hurricane against a US consensus still below prior year, Mexican construction +7.5%) add, energy at $104 Brent subtracts. I agree with rejecting the baseline's 1.33% history: real Cemex prints move 3.6-13.4%.

opus55.note: Peso about 5% stronger than the guide's FX assumption against a consensus at the guide floor (i0, company documents), plus a quiet US hurricane quarter and non-repeating Q2 one-offs (i2), net of oil-driven energy costs (i3) and soft European volumes (i4); abs move set from the confirmed earnings reactions (-8.7 to +13.4), not the 6-K-matched history.

sonnet55.note: Rests on item 0: peso 6.5% stronger than the guide's FX assumption while FY EBITDA consensus sits at the guide floor, after a 21% drawdown; baseline reaction history is unreliable, so scale comes from the name's own real prints (about 6%).

fable51.note: Rests on item 0, Cemex's own 6-K FX assumption (MXN 18.25-18.50) against a peso 4-6% stronger in its own filings while 14-analyst FY consensus sits at the guide floor, plus the quiet US hurricane season and non-repeating Q2 one-offs (item 2) against a US consensus still below prior year; energy-cost guide risk (item 3) is the main offset, and the Q2 beat-and-raise selling off -3.6% keeps p_up near 60 rather than higher; the baseline's 6-K reaction history is not an earnings scale, so abs_move is set on the real prints (-8.7, +9.9, -3.6, +6.3).

opus5.note: An honest near-wash on a name with the largest move in the pack: every negative that would make this a short is already public and telegraphed (DGCA air volumes, $100+ Brent, a stock -52% from its high with +6.56 points of put skew bid and 9.3x put/call OI), while the only genuinely unpriced items are three post-dated peer prints landing after MMYT last spoke and pointing both ways - IHCL's 2026-10-21 +21% revenue and raised FY guide into the 43%-of-margin hotels segment and ixigo's bus GTV +31.6% on the positive side, ixigo's air take rate collapsing 9.38% to 7% on the negative - with item 6's mis-specified +17% reported revenue bar the one thing that can drive a first algorithmic reaction.

opus55.note: Weak domestic air and ixigo's take-rate compression (i0, i3), a cautious oil-driven outlook (i5) and a mis-specified revenue bar set up a headline miss (i6), roughly offset by IHCL and ixigo bus read-throughs (i1, i2) and a crowded short (i4); near-balanced, slight downside lean in line with the paid skew.

sonnet55.note: Weak DGCA air volumes, ixigo's take-rate fall and a mis-specified revenue bar net against IHCL/ixigo bus and hotel read-throughs; downside skew and oil lean it modestly negative but a crowded short and low bar cap the lean.

fable51.note: Near-balanced: the IHCL and ixigo peer prints after MMYT last spoke (items 1-2) point up on hotels and bus, while telegraphed domestic-air weakness (item 0), a cautious festive outlook on $100+ oil (item 5), ixigo's air take-rate compression (item 3) and a mis-specified revenue bar (item 6) point down with the +6.6 downside skew; nothing company-level and unpriced decides it, so p_up sits just under 50 on a large implied move.

opus5.note: Rests on item 0: FHB, the only same-market peer, printed this morning after BOH's consensus was set, with margin above its own guide and interest-bearing deposit cost FALLING through a mid-quarter hike - a dated primary-document read on the exact NII line BOH trades on - but item 1 is the credit half of that same 8-K (a $20.3M provision, 0.60% NCOs) landing on a bank that disclosed its own one-borrower criticized jump, and item 5's guide-built revenue shortfall repeats the pattern that sold -4.7% last quarter, so the two halves largely offset.

opus55.note: FHB's same-day margin beat and falling Hawaii deposit costs (i0) plus a washed-out relative tape (i4) against a guide-built revenue shortfall (i5) and FHB's CRE credit read-across (i1); peer proxies that mostly offset, so a mild long lean.

sonnet55.note: Peer FHB margin and deposit-cost read-across (+) roughly offsets FHB's CRE credit hit and the small revenue-bar gap; positioning after an 11.8% relative drawdown tips it slightly up.

fable51.note: Rests on item 0, FHB's same-morning 8-K showing Hawaii deposit costs fell and margin beat its own guide after the hike, landing on BOH's NII line with consensus set before it; offset by the guide-built small revenue shortfall (item 5) and the FHB CRE credit read-across (item 1), with the hike-as-tailwind reaffirmation (item 3) and a washed-out relative tape (item 4) adding a little.
